svg.title: Tenet
svg.desc: Worlds and Thread atlas. Story order progresses downward. Connections use reserved routing space. Full relationship and citation ledgers follow the chart. The HTML companion contains the complete accessible model.
svg.text: Per-traveller direction; turnstiles fork forward and inverted strands
2.5D · cabinet axonometric · depth separates surfaces only · Story-order ranks, not elapsed time. Equal ranks do not assert physical simultaneity.
Amber S± — Split outcomes. + and − are signs, not fates.
Blue T — Directed transfers. B body · M memory · C consciousness · S signal · ? literal/unspecified mechanism.
Emerald V / L — Numbered visits and explicit links only. Emerald centre on a cable means the route follows that connection.
Slate rail — World identity. Cutoff means chart boundary, not destruction. Crossings are bridges; only markers are joins.
Evidence / fate — [n] opens the evidence record. × dead · ● alive · ? unknown · ∅ nonexistent. Purple dotted connections are annotation references.

{"id": "canon", "kind": "canon_statement", "text": "Turnstiles invert a traveller's time direction. The Protagonist recruits Neil; they run a temporal pincer
on Stalsk-12 (red team forward, blue team inverted, 10-minute offset). Neil is revealed as the soldier who died saving the Protagonist at the Kyiv opera - an
inverted strand from the future. The Algorithm is assembled and hidden in the past.", "title": "Tenet (2020), theatrical cut"}
{"id": "allocation", "kind": "test_fixture", "text": "Inverted passage is modelled as a transfer with mechanism time_travel between lane Forward and lane

are charted as separate events here.", "title": "Fixture allocations"}
